From Kostner Avenue eastward to Crawford Avenue the improvement has been swung southward slightly to avoid disturbing an extensive channelization of Butterfield Creek Tributary and two presently adequate bridges leading from Lincoln Highway into the Korvette Shopping Center on the north side of the highway.
At the Crawford Avenue/Lincoln Highway/Governor's Highway intersection several alternatives were investigated which both left the intersection as a five-way complex and separated it into two or more right-angled intersections. The recommended alternative shifts Governor's Highway to the north to intersect Crawford Avenue at a right angle opposite the Korvette Shopping Center driveway and far enough north of Lincoln Highway to provide adequate storage for the large number of vehicles making left turns onto Lincoln Highway. The resulting pair of four-way intersections improve the traffic safety as well as the traffic flow characteristics.
Moving eastward from Crawford Avenue along Lincoln Highway, the centerline of the improvement was moved to the north to avoid disturbing two adjacent cemeteries. Once past the cemeteries the centerline of the improvement swings back southward to meet the existing Lincoln Highway centerline. From this point the improvement moves along the existing centerline to Western Avenue.
At Olympian Way minor adjustments in the intersection were made to eliminate a jog, thus providing a smoother transition in north-south vehicle travel.
Another location shift occurs at the intersection of Lincoln Highway and Indiana Street where presently Indiana Street, Olympic Circle and Kedzie Street all intersect Lincoln Highway within a distance of 200 feet. This intersection was relocated as a fourway right-angled intersection to facilitate traffic safety.
